transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-08 10:00 UTC | Duration: ~45 minutes | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Luis Romero (Redwood CSM), Jordan Lee (Clarion Dir Eng), Priya Nair (Clarion ML), Samir Gupta (Clarion CTO), Elena Morales (Clarion SRE)

Summary (auto): Recap of POC results, agreement on canary/A-B ramp strategy, action items to produce updated runbook and schedule dry-run. Clarion to confirm cutover week; Redwood to provide final pricing for dedicated vs hosted.

00:00:02 - Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Uh, quick goal for today — flesh out the rollout plan, make sure the canary and A/B approaches are clear, and align on the dry-run schedule.
00:00:18 - Jordan Lee: Yep, thanks Alex. We had good perf numbers in the last test but, um, want to make sure the cutover minimizes risk. Our compliance folks also need a runbook with KMS, audit logs, and the rollback steps.
00:00:33 - Maya Patel: Great, hi all. I'll go over the suggested canary percentages and the monitoring hooks we recommend. Quick note: some transcriptions from last time said K V cache instead of KV cache, so apologies if my notes look odd.
00:01:05 - Samir Gupta: Important for us is the rollback — if latency spikes past our SLO at 99th or we see errors over 1% for 5 minutes, we need an automated fallback to the previous model and, if possible, route to hosted fallback.
00:01:24 - Alex Chen: That aligns with what we recommend. Proposed SLO triggers for canary: hold at 5% traffic for 2 hours, check 95th and 99th latency plus error rates and token cost. If everything looks green, ramp to 25% over next 6 hours, then to 50% next day and full cutover after 72 hours.
00:02:05 - Priya Nair: Can we make the ramping a bit more conservative? For healthcare, even small errors are high risk. Maybe 5% -> 15% -> 30% -> 60% with longer observation windows.
00:02:22 - Maya Patel: Totally reasonable. We can parameterize the policy. The Redwood platform supports policy-based routing so we can do region or user-segment based canaries and A/B tests.
00:02:50 - Elena Morales: On observability we need tracing for request IDs, token-level cost breakdown isn't necessary in-prod but latency histograms, error logs, and a per-route dashboard are critical. Also, who owns escalation? We need clear on-call contacts.
00:03:07 - Luis Romero: From CSM side we'll make sure the runbook has an on-call matrix; Redwood can plug into your PagerDuty/SMS and also send webhook alerts.
00:03:25 - Jordan Lee: Also, about Dedicated vs Hosted — budget constraints make hosted appealing but we worry about data residency and audit logs. Can you confirm KMS integration for hosted?
00:03:42 - Alex Chen: Yes, hosted supports customer-managed keys (KMS) for at-rest encryption in our Private offering and we have integrations for enterprise KMS in Dedicated as well. I'll include the SOC2/ISO notes in the write-up.
00:04:02 - Samir Gupta: We might want Private (VPC) if legal insists. What's the rollout difference operationally?
00:04:15 - Maya Patel: Private deployment requires a short provisioning window; typically a week for initial network setup and compliance checks. Runtime behavior and canary tooling are the same, but we'll need your infra team to open a couple ports and share peering details.
00:04:40 - Priya Nair: For the dry-run, can we schedule a night/weekend window? We expect production-like traffic patterns to surface any stateful KV cache issues and GPU memory behaviour.
00:04:55 - Maya Patel: Yes, we recommend a staged dry-run: 1) smoke tests, 2) load ramp to 50% of projected peak, 3) full load for 30 minutes. We'll provide the script.
00:05:18 - Alex Chen: I'll send the exact times and the test script. Action: Maya to produce the perf checklist.
00:05:36 - Jordan Lee: On rollback specifics, we need the following in runbook: rollback trigger thresholds, automated fallback steps, manual escalation, and data retention steps post-rollback.
00:05:52 - Maya Patel: Noted. We'll add rollback example commands and the API endpoints for invalidating caches / clearing session keys.
00:06:10 - Elena Morales: One thing — during the POC we saw a brief 500 spike when the KV cache TTL expired, maybe a race. Can we include warm-up hooks to pre-populate caches during cutover?
00:06:28 - Maya Patel: Yes, we have a cache-warming utility and can add a pre-warm step in the runbook that runs right before routing traffic. Also recommend gradual prefix-KV warming for top N users.
00:06:45 - Priya Nair: Also, when you say model fallbacks — can we pin to model versions? We don't want silent upgrades that change behavior.
00:06:58 - Alex Chen: Absolutely — you can pin model versions and only move versions via explicit rollout. We'll document that in the runbook and include checks for diffs versus your eval set.
00:07:18 - Samir Gupta: Cost question — during ramping, how does billing look? Token-based still, but does canary traffic double-count?
00:07:31 - Luis Romero: Billing is token-based for hosted; Dedicated is base capacity plus token/minor usage depending on your commit. For canary tests on hosted we can apply credits for POC; I'll include a sample estimate.
00:07:47 - Jordan Lee: Great. For compliance, we also need to know log retention windows and ability to redact PHI.
00:07:58 - Alex Chen: We'll include redaction notes. Hosted has configurable retention and audit log export; Private gives you complete control.
00:08:12 - Maya Patel: Back to the A/B approach — we recommend a control vs new pipeline A/B where control is current system and new is Redwood route. Start at 10% new pipeline for a day with comparison metrics on quality (latency, QA evals).
00:08:33 - Priya Nair: For quality measurement, we'll run our eval set each day and monitor for regressions. Can Redwood integrate eval alerts?
00:08:43 - Maya Patel: Yes — we can wire eval thresholds into alerts. We can push eval metrics to your dashboard or send periodic reports.
00:08:58 - Alex Chen: Let's talk timeline. Clarion, what's your target cutover week?
00:09:06 - Jordan Lee: We're aiming for the week of 2026-05-04 but need to confirm with product and legal. If we can't do that, late May is okay.
00:09:17 - Samir Gupta: We need at least two dry-runs before production. Prefer one internal dry-run and one live dry-run with small user segment.
00:09:28 - Maya Patel: That's doable. Proposed schedule: Week 1: infra prep and runbook finalization. Week 2: internal dry-run (staging). Week 3: live dry-run with 5-15% users. Week 4: ramp and cutover.
00:09:48 - Priya Nair: Sounds good. Who signs off for go/no-go?
00:09:52 - Jordan Lee: I'll be primary for technical sign-off, Samir will be executive sign-off and legal will give compliance greenlight.
00:10:02 - Alex Chen: Perfect. Now I'll walk through the runbook outline so we can capture any missing pieces.
00:10:10 - Alex Chen: Section 1: Pre-cutover checklist (network, certs, KMS, access, observability hooks). Section 2: Canary policy and thresholds. Section 3: Rollback procedures. Section 4: Dry-run script and perf checklist. Section 5: Contacts and escalation. Any additions?
00:10:31 - Elena Morales: Add data validation steps after cutover: spot checks on returned outputs, sampling for PHI leaks, and automated smoke tests.
00:10:44 - Maya Patel: We'll include a sampling job that compares model outputs against your guardrails. Also include an automated job for rate limiting if abnormal token usage is detected.
00:10:58 - Priya Nair: For A/B we should track both latency and semantic quality — maybe run a small human-in-the-loop evaluation for first day.
00:11:09 - Alex Chen: Yes, good idea. We'll include a lightweight HITL checklist for Day 1.
00:11:20 - Jordan Lee: Any concerns about runtime performance regression when scaling to 50%+ traffic? During POC we saw good median but 99th was marginal.
00:11:31 - Maya Patel: We'll run targeted 99th percentile tests on staging using your worst-case prompts, and if necessary we'll recommend quantization or model variant that reduces 99th tail with minimal quality loss.
00:11:48 - Samir Gupta: Can you provide recommendations on batching params? We saw some token cost spikes that might be related to small batch sizes.
00:11:58 - Maya Patel: Sure — we'll suggest batching configurations per route; Redwood Optimize can generate recommended params based on your seq length distribution.
00:12:12 - Alex Chen: Quick callout: during the POC we hit a limit in concurrent KV cache warmers. That's been fixed in the runtime but we'll validate in dry-run.
00:12:27 - Priya Nair: Good to know. Also can we get a run-of show for the cutover weekend?
00:12:33 - Luis Romero: We'll draft a run-of-show: exact timestamps, who executes each step, who validates, and expected checkpoints.
00:12:45 - Jordan Lee: And a checklist for rollback dry-run — actually practice a rollback in staging.
00:12:51 - Maya Patel: We'll include a 'practice rollback' step in the staging run.
00:12:58 - Alex Chen: Any outstanding legal items we should note?
00:13:03 - Samir Gupta: We need audit logs for three years and proof of secure deletion when requested. Also SOC2 report in place.
00:13:14 - Alex Chen: We'll attach our SOC2 and ISO docs, and include the audit log retention options in the runbook.
00:13:24 - Jordan Lee: Okay, circling back to the canary percentages — we agreed to make them conservative for healthcare. Final proposal: 5% -> 15% (12 hours) -> 30% (24 hours) -> 60% (48 hours) -> 100% after 72 hours of stable metrics. Does that work?
00:13:45 - Maya Patel: Works for us. We'll parameterize windows so you can change them if legal wants longer.
00:13:57 - Priya Nair: For alerts, set a primary alert when 99th latency > X or error rate > Y, and a secondary when token cost deviates > 20% from expected.
00:14:12 - Elena Morales: Also an alert for sudden increase in model hallucination scores from eval hooks.
00:14:19 - Maya Patel: We'll add eval-based alerts.
00:14:26 - Alex Chen: Next, A/B metrics — we'll produce a comparison dashboard showing latency percentiles, error rate, cost per 1k tokens, and quality regression score.
00:14:36 - Jordan Lee: That should be consumable by PM and execs.
00:14:40 - Samir Gupta: On the topic of scaling, if we need dedicated capacity can Redwood provision burst capacity during ramp?
00:14:50 - Maya Patel: Yes, Dedicated supports burst options; we can arrange a buffer pool for go-live if you lock a short commit. We'll include that in the pricing appendix.
00:15:03 - Luis Romero: I'll include a sample contract clause for burst capacity.
00:15:10 - Priya Nair: Any limitations on function/tool calling or streaming? We use streaming heavily.
00:15:17 - Maya Patel: Streaming is supported; watch out for tail latency on very long sessions. We'll test for that in dry-run.
00:15:26 - Jordan Lee: About telemetry — can we get per-route token breakdown by tenant?
00:15:32 - Alex Chen: Yes, token-level cost and latency per route and per API key is available in Redwood Console. We'll make sure your team has access and a dashboard template.
00:15:45 - Priya Nair: For the dry-run script, include seed data and a mix of short and long prompts to emulate production.
00:15:53 - Maya Patel: We'll provide a seed corpus and suggest a profile for traffic mix.
00:16:04 - Alex Chen: Alright, we're approaching a quarter in. Any other blockers?
00:16:10 - Elena Morales: We need confirmation of maintenance windows from infra; otherwise no blockers.
00:16:15 - Jordan Lee: I'll follow up offline with infra and legal.
00:16:19 - Samir Gupta: Also please include a simple SLA for the first 90 days post-cutover.
00:16:25 - Alex Chen: We'll include a short-term SLA addendum for the pilot and then the fuller SLA for Dedicated if you go that route.
00:16:36 - Luis Romero: Recap of action items: runbook, dry-run script, pricing appendix, schedule confirmation.
00:16:44 - Jordan Lee: Sounds good. One last question — do you have a suggested cutover hour? Midnight local or midday?
00:16:52 - Maya Patel: Night windows reduce user impact, but depends on system dependencies and staff availability. Many customers do a midnight cutover with a small ops team on call.
00:17:05 - Priya Nair: We'll check internal ops coverage.
00:17:09 - Alex Chen: Ok everyone — final check. We'll send the draft runbook by Friday, and schedule the staging dry-run week after next. Anything else?
00:17:19 - Jordan Lee: No, that's it from Clarion. Thanks.
00:17:23 - Samir Gupta: Thanks all.
00:17:26 - Alex Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up with notes and the runbook link.
00:17:30 - Luis Romero: I'll attach pricing spreadsheet and SOC2 in the follow-up.
00:17:35 - Maya Patel: I'll share the dry-run checklist and perf scripts.
00:17:40 - Alex Chen: Meeting adjourned.

(End of recording)

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker label switches and minor word errors (e.g., "K V cache"), filler words and overlaps preserved to reflect Fireflies output.
